newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees slow start to week.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees slow start to week.

text.p: New enquiry was thin on the ground at the start of the week on the sugar freight market and little firmer business was reported.
CSR quoted for 23,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for 20/30 March.
E D & F Man was open for 14,000 tonnes in bags from Acajutla to Colombo for 10/15 March and 9/11,150 tonnes from Eemshaven to Lagos, shipbrokers said.
Iran has tendered to buy another cargo of white sugar for April shipment.
In other news, a strike by warehouse workers at Brazil's key port of Santos is thought to be affecting 90 percent of imports and a smaller percentage of exports.
Some 140 workers are involved in the strike over back pay, which began earlier on Monday and is set to continue indefinitely.
China is said to have bought 22,000 tonnes of Thai raw sugar for March shipment, adding to the 14,000 tonnes which it purchased earlier this month. Mitsui and Kerry were named as the suppliers.

Traders said the Solar Glory, chartered by Mitsui, was scheduled to arrive at a Thai port on March 4 to load 12,000 tonnes while Kerry's Marina Lauri arrived in Bangkok on Sunday to pick up 10,000 tonnes in bags.
Lloyds Shipping Intelligence said the Cyprus-flagged freighter Nika II, which ran aground in gale force nine winds at Veracruz anchorage, is still aground.
The Nika II sailed from Abidjan on January 23 and was inbound to Veracruz to load bagged sugar for Algeria.
